claims.claim: 1. openProjectFromNativeDialog takes both boundaries by injection and the project read model as a generic type parameter, and imports no Runtime client
claims.evidence:
apps/desktop/src/orchestration/project-open.ts L87 `export async function openProjectFromNativeDialog

(` with parameters `selectDirectory: ProjectDirectorySelector` and `inspectProject: ProjectInspector

` (L88-L89) — both boundaries are arguments, neither is imported. The read model is the type parameter `P`, carried through both `ProjectOpenOutcome

` and `ProjectInspector

`, both declared locally in this file. No import exists at all: three independent checks agree — ast_grep pattern `import $$$` over the file returned 0 matches, read_file of the whole file shows no import statement, and `grep -n '^import\|require('` exited 1 (no match). The unit suite pins the same property from the code text: project-open.test.ts `does not import the Runtime project client` asserts the comment-stripped source has no `from "../runtime/` and `does not reach for Tauri or a dialog of its own` asserts no `@tauri-apps` and no `invoke`.

claims.claim: 2. a cancelled selection returns { status: 'cancelled' } without calling the inspector
claims.evidence: project-open.ts: `const projectPath = await selectDirectory(); if (projectPath === null) { return { status: 'cancelled' }; }` returns before the only call to `inspectProject`, so a null selection cannot reach the inspector in any code path (there is no try/catch and no second call site). Unit suite asserts it three ways: `reports a dismissed picker as a cancelled outcome` (resolves to exactly `{ status: 'cancelled' }`), `never inspects when the picker was dismissed` (recorded `seen` is empty), `carries nothing but the status in a cancelled outcome` (`Object.keys(outcome)` is `['status']`). Integration suite asserts the cross-boundary half: `returns cancelled and never asks the Runtime when the user dismisses the picker` — call count 1 for the stubbed `invoke` and `expect(fetchMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.

claims.claim: 3. the selected path is forwarded character for character
claims.evidence: project-open.ts: the value from `selectDirectory()` is bound once to `const projectPath`, tested against `null`, and handed to `inspectProject(projectPath)` and returned as `projectPath` with no transformation anywhere in the file — no trim, no separator rewrite, no case folding, no `resolve()`, no `replace()`. Unit suite pins it with `forwards the selected directory character for character` (`expect(inspection.seen[0]).toBe(PROJECT_PATH)`, strict identity, plus `toEqual`) and `normalises nothing about the selected directory` on a hostile input with leading/trailing spaces, mixed case and a `\n` sequence. The integration suite carries a hostile-but-legal path (`HOSTILE_PROJECT_PATH` with spaces, `&`, `?`, `#`, `..`) through the real bridge and the real client and asserts `outcome.projectPath` is that exact string.

claims.claim: 4. the integration test exercises the real bridge, the real orchestration and the real Runtime client, stubbing only the Tauri invoke and fetch
claims.evidence: project-open.integration.test.ts imports the real modules by value and makes no module mock of them: `selectProjectDirectory` / `SELECT_PROJECT_DIRECTORY_COMMAND` / `ProjectDirectoryBridgeError` from `../desktop/project-directory-bridge`, `inspectProject` / `RuntimeProjectApiError` / `RuntimeProjectTransportError` from `../runtime/project-client`, `openProjectFromNativeDialog` from `./project-open`. Exactly two seams are stubbed, confirmed by grep for `vi.mock|vi.stubGlobal|vi.hoisted`: one `vi.hoisted` + `vi.mock('@tauri-apps/api/core', ...)` at L30/L32 and one `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock)` at L73 (undone by `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` at L77). There is no `vi.mock` for either local module, so the chain selectProjectDirectory -> openProjectFromNativeDialog -> inspectProject is the production chain with only its two outermost adapters replaced; the Runtime/storage and the OS picker are not mocked away by a build-time fake of the modules themselves. Ran it: `npx vitest run src/orchestration/project-open.test.ts src/orchestration/project-open.integration.test.ts` → exit 0, `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 25 passed (25)` (integration file 9 tests, unit file 16 tests).

claims.claim: 5. would the integration test's path-forwarding assertion fail if the client concatenated the query string instead of encoding it?
claims.verdict: confirmed — yes, the it-block goes RED; but the kill is driven by `&` and `#`, not by encoding style as such
claims.evidence: client side: apps/desktop/src/runtime/project-client.ts L224-L225 `const query = new URLSearchParams({ project_path: projectPath }).toString(); return `${RUNTIME_URL}${PROJECT_INSPECT_PATH}?${query}`;`. Assertions under test: project-open.integration.test.ts L123 `expect(url.searchParams.get('project_path')).toBe(HOSTILE_PROJECT_PATH)`, L125 `expect(url.hash).toBe('')` (plus L121 pathname, L124 getAll length, L120 origin). Reproduced independently with node against the fixture string `C:\canx\Projects\Mixed Case & more?\#tag\..\Vehicle_Bus`: encoded query (`URLSearchParams`) → value identity true, hash '' true; raw concatenation (`'?project_path=' + path`) → `url.searchParams.get('project_path')` returns only `'C:\canx\Projects\Mixed Case '` (& terminates the value) — identity false, `url.hash` becomes `'#tag\..\Vehicle_Bus'` — false. So the first failing assertion would be L123, and L125 is independently broken too; L120/L121/L124 still pass, i.e. only the two assertions that carry the hostile characters do the killing. Also probed `encodeURI(P)` (which leaves `&` and `#` alone): identity false, hash non-empty — still RED. `encodeURIComponent(P)` on the value: passes. Conclusion: the assertion does discriminate concatenation from encoding, but only because HOSTILE_PROJECT_PATH was deliberately built to contain `&` and `#`; a path of only spaces/case/`..` would be asserted-equal under both implementations, since `URLSearchParams.get` decodes, so this test is not sensitive to `%20` vs `+` style differences.

not_confirmable: The native OS directory picker itself (the Rust `select_project_directory` command and the real filesystem dialog) — the integration suite stubs `invoke` and the file itself states the OS selection edge is owned by the Rust module's focused tests; those Rust tests were not read or run in this verification.
The real Python Runtime's HTTP answer for `GET /project/inspect?project_path=…` — `fetch` is stubbed, so the request URL is asserted but no live sidecar response was observed.

Whether the Rust half and the TypeScript half agree on the command name was only read statically (the integration suite's `the Rust and TypeScript halves name the same command` test does a source-text assertion against apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs and project_directory_bridge.rs); no cargo test was executed. Its behaviour was verified only insofar as the suite passed.
